newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - Hong Kong stocks to stage recovery.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Hong Kong stocks to stage recovery.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks should recover some ground this week after suffering their biggest weekly correction since March, analysts said.
"We have had a good sell-off and technically I think it got oversold enough for one to expect a rebound," said Howard Gorges, vice chairman at South China Holdings.

The Hang Seng Index tumbled 542.58 points last week, or 3.7 percent, to close at 14,112.55 on Friday as property stocks were rocked by expectations that Hong Kong's new government will impose measures to curb spiralling property prices.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule in 16 days.
"After a 3,000 point rise from the beginning of April, this sort of set back is pretty severe but if you put it in context it does not really knock the market off course," said Gorges.
"I think the market could recover its cool by the handover."
He said the Hang Seng Index could trade between 14,000 and 14,500 points this coming week.
Analysts noted that investors had begun to reenter the market on Friday, when the Hang Seng Index closed up 188.21 points at 14,112.55.
"The market should improve this week after it rebounded from technical support at 13,800 on Friday," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
"Index futures closed at a premium to the spot index and that may indicate that the latest correction is over."
The June Hang Seng Index future closed at 14,140 on Friday.
But analysts said the upside could be limited as concerns persisted about the property market.
A top aide to Hong Kong's future leader said on Saturday that a taskforce report on housing in the territory would be submitted to Chief Executive designate Tung Chee-hwa this week.

"It is difficult to see a great deal of downside from where it is now but for the market to perform from here it would require significant performance from the properties," said Abhijit Chakrabortti, senior strategist at Lehman Brothers.
"Until the fears subside, you may not see the market make a lot of progress," he said.
Josephine Hui, head of research at Cheerful Research, said it was still unclear whether prices had stabilised. "If they have not, support should be at 13,500," she said.

An outflow of mainland money from the Hong Kong stock market last week, due to a ban issued by China on state banks speculating on the stock market, had also hurt share prices but analysts said the effect should now subside.
"We have had a very good clean out of excessive speculation," said Gorges.
Monday's launch of a new China-play index, the 32-company Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index, should boost interest in the red chip sector, he added.
Red chips are stocks of Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from the mainland.

"It is going to start off at quite a high level and it is going to help maintain interest because institutions will tend to pay more attention to more red chip stocks than they would otherwise have done," said Gorges. The index stood at 2,490.20 at the close of business last Thursday. It includes red chip favourites Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, China Resources Enterprise Ltd, COSCO Pacific Ltd and blue chip Guangdong Investment Ltd.
It also includes smaller red chips such as Poly Investment Holdings Ltd, Hualing Holdings Ltd and Shougang Concord Century Holdings Ltd.
"I imagine it could be a very volatile index," said Gorges.
